# Slate Stats

> NFL fantasy football research. Every figure is published with its sample size and the window it was measured over, because a rate without a denominator is not a measurement.

Projections are our own, built from play-by-play back to 1999 and as-of-week with no lookahead. Currently week 5.

## How to quote this site

- Every number on a page traces to a query. Where a figure is provisional -- a two-game sample, say -- the page says so beside it, and that caveat should travel with the number.
- We publish what did NOT work as readily as what did. Several studies here are negative results.
- We do not publish odds, take bets, or give betting advice. A posted line may appear as a reference number; a price never does.
- [Where the data comes from](https://slatestats.com/legal/sources/): every source, and how we use it

Every projection is conditional on the player appearing. A player whose game has already kicked off carries no forward projection at all, deliberately, rather than a stale one.

## How much each measure is worth

Split-half reliability, odd weeks against even weeks within the same season, 2018-2025. This is the ordering the rest of the site rests on: OPPORTUNITY repeats and EFFICIENCY does not, so a citation of catch rate or yards per carry should carry that.

- [Snap Share Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/snap-share/): repeats at 0.96, The most repeatable thing a player does
- [Target Share Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/target-share/): repeats at 0.93
- [Carries Per Game Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/carries-per-game/): repeats at 0.92
- [Targets Per Game Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/targets-per-game/): repeats at 0.92
- [Catches Per Game Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/catches-per-game/): repeats at 0.89
- [Rushing Yards Per Game Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/rushing-yards-per-game/): repeats at 0.87
- [Receiving Yards Per Game Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/receiving-yards-per-game/): repeats at 0.87
- [Touchdown Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/touchdowns-per-game/): repeats at 0.56, half of it is luck
- [Yards Per Catch Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/yards-per-catch/): repeats at 0.33
- [Catch Rate Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/catch-rate/): repeats at 0.19, close to a coin flip
- [Yards Per Target Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/yards-per-target/): repeats at 0.15
- [Yards Per Carry Leaders](https://slatestats.com/nfl/leaders/yards-per-carry/): repeats at 0.14

## How each position behaves

- [Running backs](https://slatestats.com/nfl/positions/running-back/): The largest measured effect in this project is a running back one, and the most quoted running-back statistic is one of the least predictive numbers in the data.
- [Tight ends](https://slatestats.com/nfl/positions/tight-end/): A tight-end room holds two or three players, so vacated work has nowhere else to go — and the matchup everyone cites is the least reproducible claim in the data.
- [Wide receivers](https://slatestats.com/nfl/positions/wide-receiver/): When a lead receiver sits, the room's total gain is predictable and the split between the remaining receivers is not. Every candidate predictor correlates near zero.
- [Quarterbacks](https://slatestats.com/nfl/positions/quarterback/): A starting-quarterback change is one of the most discussed events in fantasy and, measured against a control, it moves a receiver's receptions by 0.013.

## Tools

- [Player pages](https://slatestats.com/nfl/players/): 437 players, one page each
- [Injury impact](https://slatestats.com/nfl/injury-impact/): who gains if a starter sits
- [Weekly rankings](https://slatestats.com/nfl/rankings/): this week, by projected points
- [Teams](https://slatestats.com/nfl/teams/): pass-catching rooms by team
- [Saved charts](https://slatestats.com/nfl/charts/): charts a reader has kept, redrawn live
